title: III. Sacraments of Old and New Testament; Cap.12 next
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWELVE follows, On ye sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament. — III. There stand as sacraments belonging toward ye Old Testament and belonging toward ye New. Before Abraham ye Church stood as without sacraments strictly so called, fed by ye word alone—though in integrity ye tree belonging toward life showed Christ with a kind belonging toward sacramental signification, and after ye fall there stood as extraordinary sacramental signs (Noah's ark, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4).
pass_b_english: III. There are sacraments of the Old Testament and of the New. Before Abraham the Church was without sacraments strictly so called, fed by the word alone—though in integrity the tree of life showed Christ with a kind of sacramental signification, and after the fall there were extraordinary sacramental signs (Noah's ark, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4).
CHAPTER TWELVE follows, On the sacraments of the Old Testament.
source_text: III. Sunt autem sacramenta alia veteris, alia Novi Testamenti. Ante Abrahamum Ecclesia fuit sine sacramentis stricte sumptis, solo verbo pasta; etiamsi in statu integritatis arbor vitae quadam sacramentali significatione Christum ostenderit, & post lapsum signa sacramentalia extraordinaria fuerunt (arca Noae, 1 Pet. 3:20-21; 1 Cor. 10:1-4). CAPUT DUODECIMUM sequitur, De sacramentis veteris testamenti.
